record.original_question: What geometric regularity can the boundary components of a Herman ring have? In particular, under what hypotheses are these boundaries Jordan curves or quasicircles, when can they have fractal structure, what can be said about their Hausdorff dimension or Lebesgue measure, and can a Herman-ring boundary ever have positive area?

evidence.quote: The geometric nature of the boundary components of Herman rings is largely mysterious. In particular, it is not known under what conditions these boundaries are Jordan curves, quasicircles, or have fractal structure. Little is known about the Hausdorff dimension or Lebesgue measure of the boundary of a Herman ring. Whether such boundaries can have positive area is an open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a rational map of degree at least $2$ acting on the Riemann sphere. The Fatou set $F(f)$ is the maximal open set on which the iterates $\{f^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ form a normal family, and its complement is the Julia set $J(f)$. A periodic Fatou component $U$ of period $p\geq 1$ is called a Herman ring if $U$ is conformally isomorphic to a round annulus $A_r=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:1<|z|<r\}$ for some $r>1$, and the first-return map $f^p:U\to U$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$ on $A_r$ for some $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$. The boundary $\partial U\subset J(f)$ consists of two disjoint connected components in $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$.

Investigate the geometric regularity of the boundary components of Herman rings of rational maps. Specifically, address the following:

(a) Under what hypotheses on $f$ (e.g., diophantine conditions on $\alpha$, the orbits of critical points, or quasiconformal surgery origins) is each boundary component of $U$ a Jordan curve? When is each boundary component a quasicircle, i.e., the image of a round circle under a quasiconformal homeomorphism of $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$?

(b) Under what conditions does a boundary component of $U$ exhibit fractal structure, in the sense of having Hausdorff dimension strictly greater than $1$?

(c) What can be said about the Hausdorff dimension and the (planar) Lebesgue measure of $\partial U$? In particular, can a boundary component of a Herman ring have strictly positive two-dimensional Lebesgue measure?
artifact.status_search_result: The geometric nature of Herman-ring boundaries remains largely unresolved. While analogous questions for Siegel disks have seen substantial progress (e.g., dimension results for quasiconformal Siegel disks, Astala's bound on quasicircle dimension), no general results determining when Herman-ring boundaries are Jordan curves/quasicircles, characterizing their Hausdorff dimension, or settling whether they can have positive Lebesgue measure appear in the literature. The problem is widely cited as open.

status_evidence.title: Dimension of the boundary of quasiconformal Siegel disks
status_evidence.snippet: Dimension results for boundaries of quasiconformal Siegel disks; analogous Herman-ring results not established.
status_evidence.claim: Related rotation-domain boundary problems are studied for Siegel disks, but corresponding Herman-ring statements remain open.

status_evidence.title: Dimension of quasicircles
status_evidence.snippet: Astala's conjecture that the Hausdorff dimension of a k-quasicircle is at most 1+k^2 was proved.
status_evidence.claim: General quasicircle dimension theory exists, but does not resolve when Herman-ring boundaries are quasicircles.
